notes: Single engine-assisted review of paired and separate Stockfish frames. References were saved before candidate output was read.

cases.rationale: After Re8, White's f6 push draws Black's g-pawn off the g-file. Both stronger Qd8 branches meet f6 with Bf8 and keep the kingside cover. The later White capture differs across the weaker branches.
Nf6+ changes the order of the exchanges. The hxg4 branches disagree about whether White should immediately recapture on g4 or switch back to the knight check.
The bishop sacrifice Bxg3 opens a sequence of rook checks after Re1. Bxg3 also works against Qh1, with a different continuation, and both moves lose decisively.
After a5, e6 draws the f-pawn off its file, Bxg7 takes a second pawn from the king's cover, and Qxh5 takes the rook. Both stronger Ne8 lines keep more cover at that stage.
Qe7 allows hxg6 and prompts fxg6 in both weaker lines, depleting the central king's pawn cover. After gxh5, Black keeps the f-pawn on its file in both searches over the corresponding exchanges.
Nxg3 draws the f-pawn away and allows Rxe3. This sequence also appears after hxg5 but White inserts Rh1 and keeps an attack. Independent long-term concession is uncertain.
Bxh3 gxh3 clears the g-file for Qg5+ and a series of checks. Qf3 also permits a g-pawn recapture, but it first trades queens and avoids the exposed king with queens on.
gxf5 opens the g-file toward Black's king. White forces Kh8 and doubles rooks against it in both searches, with the move order varying. Nd5 keeps that file closed in the early reply.
Re7 allows fxg6 and Nxh5+ before White advances the g-pawn with check. exf5 eliminates the f5-pawn first and leaves Black's g6/h5 shelter standing at that stage.
Rg7 misses the available Qxb1, which wins a rook even after White's checks. Black remains won either way and a distinct positional concession is uncertain.
gxf6 opens the g-file in front of Black's king and leaves weak f-pawns. Qxf6 keeps the g-pawn and retains kingside cover in both better lines.

Qc2 lets Black attack the kingside with h5. Both weaker lines show pressure or capture against White's kingside pawns. Nc5 keeps play away from the king during that window; the exact tactical sequence differs.
The push e6 and played gxf4 both keep a winning score. A pawn-cover change does not establish a consequential error here.
fxg5 is the engine's preferred move and exchanges the bishop for the knight without a consequential played-move loss.
hxg5 is the engine's preferred move and leaves a balanced game. The opened file is insufficient evidence of a mistake.
gxf3 is the engine's chosen defense. Bxd5 and Nxf3+ exploit the position already on the board.
Nc6 is the engine's chosen move. Re1+ in the variation is not evidence of a played-move loss.
g5 and the actual Bc7 both leave a balanced rook-versus-bishop ending. The pawn geometry does not establish a meaningful error.
